label: Q-03
severityRationale:
MOVED to QA. C4 is explicit that unused view functions are QA at best, and these are entire unused VIEW CONTRACTS: DepositView.sol and DepositPageView.sol have zero deployers, no script constructs them, and their names sit in extract-addresses.js DROPPED_CONTRACT_NAMES as a deliberate revival guard.

THE ARGUMENT FOR LOW, weighed and rejected: the sanitizer correctly refused to filter this as a plain 'unused view function' report, because there IS a concrete demonstrated root cause - both are typed against the V1/V2-shaped IPhlimbo whose 3-tuple userInfo SILENTLY MIS-DECODES PhlimboV3's 4-tuple rather than reverting, and the ABIs are still published in wagmi.config.ts. A silent mis-decode is genuinely worse than a revert, and that distinction is what keeps this from being dead-code noise. It is preserved. But realising the hazard requires a consumer to deploy or wire one of these against V3 - i.e. future code that does not exist. C4 excludes speculation on future code from H/M, and the demonstrated root cause earns the finding a place in the report, not an elevated label. QA is exactly that place.

CROSS-LINK THAT MUST NOT BE LOST IN THE QA MOVE: DepositPageView is simultaneously the subject of ledger 6b63ef6516ac (run-24 M-01, label L-07, status FIX-PENDING, entryPoint promotion-ready:broadcast) - a live view bound to the wrong phlimbo generation. So the same contract is orphaned here and owed a fix there. Those are different defects at different entry points and must not be collapsed, but a reader of the QA entry needs to know the other exists - a 'delete both sources' remediation on this QA item would interact with a fix-pending Medium-history entry elsewhere. Preserve the cross-link explicitly.

The recommendation is carried verbatim; note that its 'retype against IPhlimboV3, which will not compile against the 3-tuple' option is the compile-time impossibility that would close the hazard permanently, and is preferable to deletion precisely because of the cross-link above.
